stories.title: Will Japan rewire global rare earth supply chains with its deep-sea breakthrough?
stories.summary: Japan successfully extracted rare earth elements from seabed 5,600 metres deep near Minamitorishima, aiming to reduce dependence on China’s rare earth supply. The seabed clay is rich in critical minerals like yttrium and neodymium, vital for tech industries, with less radioactive elements than Chinese deposits. Challenges remain in processing and economic viability, but Japan seeks US partnership to secure its supply chain. Japan’s successful, world-first mission to extract rare earth deposits from the seabed at depths of nearly 5,600m beneath the Pacific surface – far deeper than Mount Fuji is tall – has ignited fresh optimism that Tokyo can break Beijing’s grip on critical mineral supply chains. The clay-like sludge pumped up from the abyssal depths surrounding Minamitorishima, Japan’s easternmost point located 1,950km southeast of Tokyo, is remarkably rich in highly coveted medium and heavy rare-earth elements.

stories.summary: While the US and some European governments view China’s vast production of electric vehicles and green-energy tech as overcapacity, African companies see it as an opportunity to secure EV technology and develop the industry. stories.title: Hong Kong police arrest 2 men allegedly linked to HK$500,000 phishing scam
stories.summary: Hong Kong police have arrested two men suspected of using 110 SIM cards in a hotel room to send phishing messages, conning victims of more than HK$500,000 (US$63,766). The force said on Saturday that the men, aged 31 and 44, were arrested last Thursday on suspicion of conspiracy to defraud. stories.title: Chinese man reunites with family after 25 years in total isolation to honour a promise
stories.summary: A Chinese man in his 60s has finally reunited with his family after spending 25 years in isolation to care for a house deep in the mountains, even after the owner had forgotten about it. Li Guoyou, 63, recently received his renewed hukou booklet, China’s official household registration, at a police station in Pingtan, a town in southwestern Sichuan province.
